task: Build a molecule-level literature dataset of dermal exposure and skin penetration evidence. Include skin permeability coefficients, transdermal flux, lag time, dermal absorption, skin retention, tape-stripping results, diffusion-cell experiments, formulation-dependent penetration, and experimentally reported skin exposure.
task_instantiation:
Extract molecule-level evidence of dermal exposure or movement into, within, retained by, or across skin. In scope are explicitly reported skin permeability coefficients (Kp/Papp), transdermal or transepidermal flux, lag time, cumulative permeated amount, percent/dose absorbed or penetrated, skin or stratum-corneum retention/deposition, tape-stripping results, receptor-fluid or dermal-microdialysate measurements attributable to skin application, quantitative formulation-dependent penetration/enhancement, and experimentally measured external skin exposure or dermally applied dose. Include in vitro/ex vivo skin diffusion-cell studies, in vivo dermal studies, human dermal exposure monitoring, and skin-mimetic permeability assays only when the result is explicitly presented as skin permeability/penetration evidence. Estimated or calculated Kp values are allowed when explicitly reported as such.

Create one record for each primary molecule × experimental condition × result metric. If one condition reports several metrics (for example flux, cumulative amount, and percent crossed), emit separate records for each metric. If the same metric is reported for distinct formulations, skin preparations/species, anatomical sites, time points, occlusion states, or interventions, emit separate records. Use the molecule's identifier as top-level `global_identifier`; do not put the molecule name in `extracted`. A named chemical class may be the primary entity for a genuine class-level claim. For mixtures or formulations, attribute a result to a molecule only when that molecule is explicitly the penetrant/analyte; do not treat excipients or formulation ingredients as penetrants merely because their composition is listed.

Require direct evidence in the text/table: an explicit numeric result, an explicit qualitative penetration/absorption statement (for example “very low” or “a small portion traversed”), or a quantitative relative effect such as a stated fold enhancement. Preserve inequalities, ranges, uncertainty, and scientific-notation multipliers in `result_value`; do not invent or algebraically derive values. Values directly readable from tables are allowed. For comparative claims, extract only if a quantitative factor/difference is stated or if the passage also provides an absolute target result; skip bare rankings and unsupported “greater than” claims. Put the comparator in `extra_details` for a relative result.

Exclude product/composite concentrations that are not tied to actual skin contact or dermal application; formulation recipes without a penetration/exposure result; TEWL or other barrier-function measurements without a chemical penetrant result; endogenous sweat/sebum concentrations; oral/inhalation/aggregate multi-route exposure estimates; toxicity endpoints such as dermal LD50, irritation, sensitization, or inflammation; intradermal/subcutaneous injection; pharmacodynamic effects; metabolism/excretion alone; and physicochemical properties (Kow, solubility) except as ancillary details to an in-scope skin result. Do not infer dermal absorption merely because a substance was applied to skin or detected systemically unless the passage attributes the finding to dermal uptake.

Interpret an unqualified claim under the study's ordinary reported conditions. Record routine context in `study_design`, `skin_source`, `formulation_vehicle`, and `exposure_time`. Put only materially exceptional conditions that alter generalizability—such as damaged/stripped skin, disease skin, enhancer pretreatment, decontamination, unusual heating, or barrier disruption—in `qualifying_conditions`; use null when none is stated. Occlusion and other important routine setup details may go in `extra_details`.

schema_spec.name: evidence_type
schema_spec.description: The single dermal result metric represented by this record. `dermally_applied_dose` requires an actual experimental skin application; `skin_exposure_measurement` is measured chemical on the skin surface or in a skin-linked exposure sample.

schema_spec.name: result_value
schema_spec.description: Reported value for the selected metric as a string; preserve qualifiers, ranges, ± uncertainty, and scientific-notation multipliers. For qualitative evidence, use the authors' concise wording. Do not calculate a value.

schema_spec.name: result_unit
schema_spec.description: Unit exactly associated with `result_value`, normalized only typographically; null for unitless or qualitative results.

schema_spec.name: study_design
schema_spec.description: Overall evidence design. Use `ex_vivo` for excised skin studies not described as diffusion-cell work; use `calculated_or_estimated` for explicitly modeled/calculated Kp rather than direct measurement.

schema_spec.name: skin_source
schema_spec.description: Species, skin preparation, and anatomical site relevant to the result, such as 'human full-thickness abdominal skin' or 'equine split skin'; null if unstated.

schema_spec.name: formulation_vehicle
schema_spec.description: Test formulation, product, vehicle, concentration, and comparator formulation when explicitly tied to the result; null if unstated.

schema_spec.name: exposure_time
schema_spec.description: Application duration, sampling time, or time point associated with the result, including units; null if unstated.

schema_spec.name: qualifying_conditions
schema_spec.description: Materially exceptional conditions affecting generalizability, such as damaged skin, enhancer pretreatment, decontamination, barrier disruption, or unusual heating. Null for standard/unqualified conditions.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Free-form string for additional details that do not fit other top-level fields.
